# Add frame level operations to enhanced multi-frame instances

Add a `pydicom.multiframe` module, the same objects also reachable from `pydicom`, holding `frame_attributes(ds, index)`, `varying_attributes(ds)`, `extract_frames(ds, indices)`, `merge_frames(datasets)`, `group_frames(ds, keys)`, `sort_frames(ds, keys)` and `MultiFrameError`. All six reject the same malformed instances. `MultiFrameError`, a `ValueError`, is raised for a dataset with no per-frame groups, empty counting as none, transfer syntax, SOP class or instance UID, not exactly one pixel data element, a shared group sequence present but not holding one item, a frame count absent or disagreeing, pixel data too short or malformed, a missing frame, an empty or repeating selection, no keys, a key that is not an attribute name or tag, incomparable values, and uncombinable inputs.

`frame_attributes` returns the attributes in the macros applying to one zero-based frame, the shared macros written first and the frame's own second, a per-frame macro replacing the shared macro carrying its tag. It is a copy, so the instance is unaffected. `varying_attributes` returns the tags whose effective value is not the same for every frame, nothing for one frame.

`extract_frames` keeps the frames `indices` names, in order. `merge_frames` takes every frame of its inputs, one or more, which must agree on SOP class, transfer syntax, pixel data element and image pixel attributes. `group_frames` returns a list of one instance per distinct combination of the effective values of `keys`, in first-appearance order, keeping their old order, frames carrying none grouping together, even when that is every frame. `sort_frames` puts them in ascending order of those values, first key first, missing values last, ties as they were. Multi-valued attributes order value by value.

A derived instance carries one shared group. In-stack positions are renumbered from one within each stack, in frame order, among those carrying them. Among the frames carrying index values, described or not, a dimension every one of them reaches with one value is then dropped, from the dimension index description and from those frames; one they do not all reach is kept. A frame's values element goes when it empties, its macro stays; the description goes when nothing is left in it. What remains is renumbered, each alone, to 1, 2, 3 in first-seen order. Only then is a macro with the same value for every frame stored once, in the shared group, every other in each frame's own. A macro may hold several items. Its pixel data element is rebuilt in the new frame order, one-bit data packed and measured in bits, not bytes, encapsulated again if it was, its length left undefined, padded to an even length if not, any extended offset table dropped. It takes a new SOP instance UID, its file meta naming that and its SOP class, and a source image sequence holding one item per input, in input order, naming its SOP class, instance UID and the 1-based frame numbers taken from it, in result order. Whatever else it carries comes from the first input, copied. Inputs are unchanged and share nothing with the result.

Implemented enhanced multi-frame operations in [multiframe.py](/app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py), with top-level exports in [__init__.py](/app/src/pydicom/__init__.py) and focused tests in [test_multiframe.py](/app/tests/test_multiframe.py).

Validation:

- Focused tests: 382 passed.
- Full suite: 2649 passed; one unrelated data-download failure due to the environment’s invalid CA bundle.

*** Add File: /app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py
+# Copyright 2008-2026 pydicom authors. See LICENSE file for details.
+"""Operations on enhanced multi-frame image instances.
+
+The functions in this module operate on the functional group macros and the
+pixel data of an enhanced multi-frame instance without decoding compressed
+pixel data.  They deliberately validate the whole instance before doing any
+work; this is important because a malformed functional group or pixel data
+element can otherwise be very easy to copy into a new, equally malformed
+instance.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from io import BufferedIOBase
+from numbers import Integral
+from struct import unpack_from
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydicom.dataelem import DataElement
+from pydicom.datadict import tag_for_keyword
+from pydicom.dataset import Dataset
+from pydicom.encaps import encapsulate
+from pydicom.fileutil import reset_buffer_position
+from pydicom.sequence import Sequence
+from pydicom.tag import BaseTag, Tag
+from pydicom.uid import UID, generate_uid
+
+
+_SHARED_FG = Tag(0x52009229)
+_PER_FRAME_FG = Tag(0x52009230)
+_NUMBER_OF_FRAMES = Tag(0x00280008)
+_DIMENSION_INDEX = Tag(0x00209222)
+_FRAME_CONTENT = Tag(0x00209111)
+_IN_STACK_POSITION = Tag(0x00209057)
+_STACK_ID = Tag(0x00209056)
+_DIMENSION_VALUES = Tag(0x00209157)
+_SOURCE_IMAGE = Tag(0x00082112)
+_EXTENDED_OFFSET = Tag(0x7FE00001)
+_EXTENDED_LENGTHS = Tag(0x7FE00002)
+
+_PIXEL_TAGS = (
+    Tag(0x7FE00008),  # Float Pixel Data
+    Tag(0x7FE00009),  # Double Float Pixel Data
+    Tag(0x7FE00010),  # Pixel Data
+)
+
+# These are the Image Pixel module attributes which describe the encoding of
+# native pixel data.  Number of Frames is intentionally excluded because it is
+# allowed to differ between inputs to merge_frames().
+_IMAGE_PIXEL_TAGS = (
+    Tag(0x00280002),  # Samples per Pixel
+    Tag(0x00280003),  # Samples per Pixel Used
+    Tag(0x00280004),  # Photometric Interpretation
+    Tag(0x00280005),  # Image Dimensions
+    Tag(0x00280006),  # Planar Configuration
+    Tag(0x00280010),  # Rows
+    Tag(0x00280011),  # Columns
+    Tag(0x00280012),  # Planes
+    Tag(0x00280014),  # Ultrasound Color Data Present
+    Tag(0x00280100),  # Bits Allocated
+    Tag(0x00280101),  # Bits Stored
+    Tag(0x00280102),  # High Bit
+    Tag(0x00280103),  # Pixel Representation
+)
+
+_MISSING = object()
+
+
+class MultiFrameError(ValueError):
+    """Raised when an enhanced multi-frame operation cannot be performed."""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _Validated:
+    """The checked parts of one input instance."""
+
+    dataset: Dataset
+    transfer_syntax: UID
+    sop_class: UID | str
+    sop_instance: UID | str
+    frame_count: int
+    pixel_tag: BaseTag
+    pixel_vr: str
+    encapsulated: bool
+    # For native data these are the frame bytes, except when ``bit_frames`` is
+    # true, in which case each entry contains one byte per pixel with values 0
+    # or 1.  Keeping the unpacked representation makes frame boundaries
+    # correct even when a frame does not end on a byte boundary.
+    frames: list[bytes]
+    bit_frames: bool
+    image_pixel: dict[BaseTag, DataElement | None]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _Selected:
+    source: _Validated
+    index: int
+    attributes: Dataset
+
+
+def _fail(message: str) -> None:
+    raise MultiFrameError(message)
+
+
+def _get_element(ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag) -> DataElement | None:
+    """Return a converted element without treating an empty value as absent."""
+    if tag not in ds._dict:
+        return None
+
+    try:
+        elem = ds[tag]
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"Unable to read element {tag}") from exc
+
+    if not isinstance(elem, DataElement):
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"Element {tag} is not a data element")
+
+    return elem
+
+
+def _value_bytes(elem: DataElement, description: str) -> bytes:
+    """Return an element's binary value without changing a buffer position."""
+    value = elem.value
+    if isinstance(value, BufferedIOBase):
+        try:
+            with reset_buffer_position(value):
+                value.seek(0)
+                data = value.read()
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(f"The {description} value is not readable") from exc
+    elif isinstance(value, bytes):
+        data = value
+    elif isinstance(value, bytearray | memoryview):
+        data = bytes(value)
+    else:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The {description} value is not binary data")
+
+    if not isinstance(data, bytes):
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The {description} value is not binary data")
+
+    return data
+
+
+def _uid_from_element(
+    ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag, description: str, *, transfer_syntax: bool = False
+) -> UID | str:
+    elem = _get_element(ds, tag)
+    if elem is None or elem.is_empty:
+        _fail(f"The dataset has no {description}")
+
+    value = elem.value
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) or value is None or not str(value).strip():
+        _fail(f"The dataset has no {description}")
+
+    try:
+        uid = UID(str(value))
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The dataset has an invalid {description}") from exc
+
+    if transfer_syntax and not uid.is_transfer_syntax:
+        _fail("The dataset has no valid Transfer Syntax UID")
+
+    return uid
+
+
+def _sequence_items(
+    ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag, description: str, *, exactly: int | None = None
+) -> list[Dataset] | None:
+    elem = _get_element(ds, tag)
+    if elem is None:
+        return None
+
+    if elem.VR != "SQ" or not isinstance(elem.value, Sequence):
+        _fail(f"The {description} is not a sequence")
+
+    items = list(elem.value)
+    if exactly is not None and len(items) != exactly:
+        _fail(f"The {description} does not contain exactly {exactly} item(s)")
+
+    if any(not isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in items):
+        _fail(f"The {description} contains a non-dataset item")
+
+    return items
+
+
+def _validate_macro_dataset(item: Dataset, description: str) -> None:
+    """Validate that a functional-group item contains usable macro sequences."""
+    for elem in item:
+        if not isinstance(elem, DataElement) or elem.VR != "SQ":
+            _fail(f"The {description} contains a non-macro element")
+        if not isinstance(elem.value, Sequence) or any(
+            not isinstance(macro_item, Dataset) for macro_item in elem.value
+        ):
+            _fail(f"The {description} contains a malformed macro")
+
+
+def _positive_int(ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag, description: str) -> int:
+    elem = _get_element(ds, tag)
+    if elem is None or elem.is_empty:
+        _fail(f"The dataset has no {description}")
+
+    value = elem.value
+    if isinstance(value, bool) or isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+        _fail(f"The dataset has an invalid {description}")
+
+    try:
+        result = int(value)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The dataset has an invalid {description}") from exc
+
+    if result <= 0:
+        _fail(f"The dataset has an invalid {description}")
+
+    return result
+
+
+def _parse_int_list(value: Any) -> list[Any]:
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, Sequence)):
+        return list(value)
+    return [value]
+
+
+def _same_value(first: Any, second: Any) -> bool:
+    """Compare DICOM values, including nested datasets and optional arrays."""
+    if first is second:
+        return True
+
+    if isinstance(first, Dataset) or isinstance(second, Dataset):
+        if not isinstance(first, Dataset) or not isinstance(second, Dataset):
+            return False
+        if list(first.keys()) != list(second.keys()):
+            return False
+        return all(_same_element(first[tag], second[tag]) for tag in first.keys())
+
+    if isinstance(first, (list, tuple, Sequence)) or isinstance(
+        second, (list, tuple, Sequence)
+    ):
+        if not isinstance(first, (list, tuple, Sequence)) or not isinstance(
+            second, (list, tuple, Sequence)
+        ):
+            return False
+        if len(first) != len(second):
+            return False
+        return all(_same_value(a, b) for a, b in zip(first, second))
+
+    try:
+        result = first == second
+        if isinstance(result, bool):
+            return result
+        return bool(result)
+    except Exception:
+        # Numpy arrays are optional and deliberately not imported by this
+        # module.  Their common equality API is still handled here without
+        # making numpy a dependency.
+        try:
+            return first.shape == second.shape and bool((first == second).all())
+        except Exception:
+            return False
+
+
+def _same_element(first: DataElement, second: DataElement) -> bool:
+    return (
+        first.tag == second.tag
+        and first.VR == second.VR
+        and _same_value(first.value, second.value)
+    )
+
+
+def _read_extended_offsets(ds: Dataset, frame_count: int) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]] | None:
+    offset_elem = _get_element(ds, _EXTENDED_OFFSET)
+    length_elem = _get_element(ds, _EXTENDED_LENGTHS)
+    if offset_elem is None and length_elem is None:
+        return None
+    if offset_elem is None or length_elem is None:
+        _fail("The Extended Offset Table is incomplete")
+
+    offsets_raw = _value_bytes(offset_elem, "Extended Offset Table")
+    lengths_raw = _value_bytes(length_elem, "Extended Offset Table Lengths")
+    if not offsets_raw or not lengths_raw:
+        _fail("The Extended Offset Table is empty")
+    if len(offsets_raw) % 8 or len(lengths_raw) % 8:
+        _fail("The Extended Offset Table has an invalid length")
+
+    offsets = [
+        unpack_from("<Q", offsets_raw, offset)[0]
+        for offset in range(0, len(offsets_raw), 8)
+    ]
+    lengths = [
+        unpack_from("<Q", lengths_raw, offset)[0]
+        for offset in range(0, len(lengths_raw), 8)
+    ]
+    if len(offsets) != frame_count or len(lengths) != frame_count:
+        _fail("The Extended Offset Table does not match the frame count")
+
+    return offsets, lengths
+
+
+def _parse_encapsulated(
+    data: bytes, frame_count: int, extended: tuple[list[int], list[int]] | None
+) -> list[bytes]:
+    """Parse encapsulated pixel data and return exactly one value per frame."""
+    if len(data) < 8:
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data is too short")
+
+    # Encapsulation is always little endian, independently of the transfer
+    # syntax used for the enclosing data set.
+    tag = unpack_from("<I", data, 0)[0]
+    if tag != 0xFFFEE000:
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data has no Basic Offset Table")
+    bot_length = unpack_from("<I", data, 4)[0]
+    if bot_length == 0xFFFFFFFF or bot_length % 4 or 8 + bot_length > len(data):
+        _fail("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+
+    bot_raw = data[8 : 8 + bot_length]
+    bot = [
+        unpack_from("<I", bot_raw, offset)[0]
+        for offset in range(0, len(bot_raw), 4)
+    ]
+    if bot and len(bot) != frame_count:
+        _fail("The Basic Offset Table does not match the frame count")
+
+    position = 8 + bot_length
+    fragment_start = position
+    fragments: list[bytes] = []
+    fragment_positions: list[int] = []
+    found_delimiter = False
+    while position < len(data):
+        if len(data) - position < 8:
+            _fail("The encapsulated pixel data is truncated")
+        item_tag = unpack_from("<I", data, position)[0]
+        item_length = unpack_from("<I", data, position + 4)[0]
+        if item_tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
+            if item_length != 0:
+                _fail("The encapsulated pixel data delimiter is malformed")
+            position += 8
+            found_delimiter = True
+            break
+        if item_tag != 0xFFFEE000 or item_length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
+            _fail("The encapsulated pixel data contains a malformed item")
+        value_start = position + 8
+        value_end = value_start + item_length
+        if value_end > len(data):
+            _fail("The encapsulated pixel data item is truncated")
+        fragments.append(data[value_start:value_end])
+        fragment_positions.append(position - fragment_start)
+        position = value_end
+
+    # The value of an undefined-length Pixel Data element normally has a
+    # delimiter written by the file writer, while encapsulate() returns the
+    # value before that delimiter.  Both forms are valid input here.
+    if found_delimiter and position != len(data):
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data has trailing bytes")
+    if not fragments or any(not fragment for fragment in fragments):
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data contains no complete frames")
+
+    if bot:
+        if bot[0] != 0 or any(a >= b for a, b in zip(bot, bot[1:])):
+            _fail("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+        if any(offset not in fragment_positions for offset in bot):
+            _fail("The Basic Offset Table points to a missing fragment")
+        starts = [fragment_positions.index(offset) for offset in bot]
+        frames = []
+        for index, start in enumerate(starts):
+            end = starts[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(starts) else len(fragments)
+            frame = b"".join(fragments[start:end])
+            if not frame:
+                _fail("The encapsulated pixel data contains a missing frame")
+            frames.append(frame)
+        return frames
+
+    if extended is not None:
+        offsets, lengths = extended
+        if offsets[0] != 0 or any(a >= b for a, b in zip(offsets, offsets[1:])):
+            _fail("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+        frames = []
+        for offset, length in zip(offsets, lengths):
+            if offset not in fragment_positions:
+                _fail("The Extended Offset Table points to a missing fragment")
+            fragment_index = fragment_positions.index(offset)
+            if fragment_index + 1 >= len(fragment_positions) and offset + 8 + length > len(
+                data
+            ):
+                _fail("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+            if len(fragments[fragment_index]) != length:
+                _fail("The Extended Offset Table length is incorrect")
+            frames.append(fragments[fragment_index])
+        return frames
+
+    if len(fragments) == frame_count:
+        return fragments
+    if frame_count == 1:
+        return [b"".join(fragments)]
+
+    # With neither offset table, multiple fragments can only be divided when
+    # the encoded stream provides a recognizable end-of-frame marker.  This
+    # covers the JPEG family and rejects ambiguous data rather than guessing.
+    frames = []
+    current: list[bytes] = []
+    for fragment in fragments:
+        current.append(fragment)
+        if b"\xff\xd9" in fragment[-10:]:
+            frames.append(b"".join(current))
+            current = []
+    if current:
+        frames.append(b"".join(current))
+    if len(frames) != frame_count or any(not frame for frame in frames):
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data does not contain the frame count")
+    return frames
+
+
+def _native_frames(
+    data: bytes,
+    frame_count: int,
+    samples: int,
+    rows: int,
+    columns: int,
+    pixel_tag: BaseTag,
+    bits_allocated: int | None,
+    photometric: Any,
+) -> tuple[list[bytes], bool]:
+    pixels_per_frame = samples * rows * columns
+    if pixel_tag == Tag(0x7FE00008):
+        bytes_per_sample = 4
+        bits_allocated = 32
+    elif pixel_tag == Tag(0x7FE00009):
+        bytes_per_sample = 8
+        bits_allocated = 64
+    elif bits_allocated == 1:
+        total_bits = pixels_per_frame * frame_count
+        expected = (total_bits + 7) // 8
+        if len(data) not in (expected, expected + (expected % 2)):
+            _fail("The pixel data length is too short or malformed")
+        if expected % 2 == 0 and len(data) != expected:
+            _fail("The pixel data length is malformed")
+
+        values = bytes(
+            (data[position // 8] >> (position % 8)) & 1
+            for position in range(total_bits)
+        )
+        return [
+            values[start : start + pixels_per_frame]
+            for start in range(0, total_bits, pixels_per_frame)
+        ], True
+    else:
+        if bits_allocated is None or bits_allocated <= 0 or bits_allocated % 8:
+            _fail("The dataset has invalid Bits Allocated")
+        bytes_per_sample = bits_allocated // 8
+
+    frame_length = pixels_per_frame * bytes_per_sample
+    if photometric == "YBR_FULL_422" and pixel_tag == Tag(0x7FE00010):
+        if samples != 3:
+            _fail("The dataset has invalid YBR_FULL_422 pixel attributes")
+        frame_length = frame_length * 2 // 3
+    expected = frame_length * frame_count
+    if len(data) not in (expected, expected + (expected % 2)):
+        _fail("The pixel data length is too short or malformed")
+    if expected % 2 == 0 and len(data) != expected:
+        _fail("The pixel data length is malformed")
+    return [
+        data[start : start + frame_length]
+        for start in range(0, expected, frame_length)
+    ], False
+
+
+def _validate(ds: Dataset) -> _Validated:
+    """Validate an enhanced multi-frame instance and return pixel metadata."""
+    try:
+        if not isinstance(ds, Dataset):
+            _fail("The object is not a DICOM dataset")
+
+        file_meta = getattr(ds, "file_meta", None)
+        if not isinstance(file_meta, Dataset):
+            _fail("The dataset has no file meta information")
+        transfer_elem = _get_element(file_meta, Tag(0x00020010))
+        if transfer_elem is None or transfer_elem.is_empty:
+            _fail("The dataset has no Transfer Syntax UID")
+        transfer_value = transfer_elem.value
+        if transfer_value is None or isinstance(transfer_value, (list, tuple)):
+            _fail("The dataset has no Transfer Syntax UID")
+        try:
+            transfer_syntax = UID(str(transfer_value))
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("The dataset has an invalid Transfer Syntax UID") from exc
+        if not transfer_syntax.is_transfer_syntax:
+            _fail("The dataset has no valid Transfer Syntax UID")
+
+        sop_class = _uid_from_element(ds, Tag(0x00080016), "SOP Class UID")
+        sop_instance = _uid_from_element(ds, Tag(0x00080018), "SOP Instance UID")
+
+        shared = _sequence_items(
+            ds, _SHARED_FG, "Shared Functional Groups Sequence", exactly=1
+        )
+        if shared is not None:
+            _validate_macro_dataset(shared[0], "Shared Functional Groups Sequence")
+
+        per_frame = _sequence_items(ds, _PER_FRAME_FG, "Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence")
+        if not per_frame:
+            _fail("The dataset has no per-frame functional groups")
+        for index, item in enumerate(per_frame):
+            _validate_macro_dataset(item, f"Per-Frame Functional Groups item {index}")
+
+        number_of_frames = _positive_int(ds, _NUMBER_OF_FRAMES, "Number of Frames")
+        if number_of_frames != len(per_frame):
+            _fail("Number of Frames disagrees with the per-frame functional groups")
+
+        pixel_tags = [tag for tag in _PIXEL_TAGS if tag in ds._dict]
+        if len(pixel_tags) != 1:
+            _fail("The dataset must contain exactly one pixel data element")
+        pixel_tag = pixel_tags[0]
+        pixel_elem = _get_element(ds, pixel_tag)
+        if pixel_elem is None:
+            _fail("The dataset has no pixel data element")
+        pixel_data = _value_bytes(pixel_elem, "pixel data")
+
+        # Validate the dimensions needed to determine native frame boundaries.
+        samples = _positive_int(ds, Tag(0x00280002), "Samples per Pixel")
+        rows = _positive_int(ds, Tag(0x00280010), "Rows")
+        columns = _positive_int(ds, Tag(0x00280011), "Columns")
+        photometric_elem = _get_element(ds, Tag(0x00280004))
+        if photometric_elem is None or photometric_elem.is_empty:
+            _fail("The dataset has no Photometric Interpretation")
+        photometric = photometric_elem.value
+
+        bits_elem = _get_element(ds, Tag(0x00280100))
+        bits_allocated: int | None = None
+        if bits_elem is not None and not bits_elem.is_empty:
+            try:
+                bits_allocated = int(bits_elem.value)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                raise MultiFrameError("The dataset has invalid Bits Allocated") from exc
+
+        extended = _read_extended_offsets(ds, number_of_frames)
+        encapsulated = transfer_syntax.is_encapsulated
+        if encapsulated:
+            if pixel_tag != Tag(0x7FE00010):
+                _fail("Only Pixel Data can be encapsulated")
+            frames = _parse_encapsulated(pixel_data, number_of_frames, extended)
+            bit_frames = False
+        else:
+            if extended is not None:
+                _fail("A native pixel data element cannot have an Extended Offset Table")
+            frames, bit_frames = _native_frames(
+                pixel_data,
+                number_of_frames,
+                samples,
+                rows,
+                columns,
+                pixel_tag,
+                bits_allocated,
+                photometric,
+            )
+
+        if len(frames) != number_of_frames or any(not frame for frame in frames):
+            _fail("The pixel data does not contain every frame")
+
+        image_pixel = {
+            tag: copy.deepcopy(_get_element(ds, tag)) for tag in _IMAGE_PIXEL_TAGS
+        }
+
+        dimension_index = _sequence_items(
+            ds, _DIMENSION_INDEX, "Dimension Index Sequence"
+        )
+        if dimension_index is not None and any(
+            not isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in dimension_index
+        ):
+            _fail("The Dimension Index Sequence is malformed")
+
+        return _Validated(
+            dataset=ds,
+            transfer_syntax=transfer_syntax,
+            sop_class=sop_class,
+            sop_instance=sop_instance,
+            frame_count=number_of_frames,
+            pixel_tag=pixel_tag,
+            pixel_vr=pixel_elem.VR,
+            encapsulated=encapsulated,
+            frames=frames,
+            bit_frames=bit_frames,
+            image_pixel=image_pixel,
+        )
+    except MultiFrameError:
+        raise
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The dataset is malformed") from exc
+
+
+def _frame_attributes_from_validated(info: _Validated, index: int) -> Dataset:
+    shared = _sequence_items(info.dataset, _SHARED_FG, "Shared Functional Groups Sequence")
+    per_frame = _sequence_items(
+        info.dataset, _PER_FRAME_FG, "Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence"
+    )
+    if per_frame is None or index < 0 or index >= len(per_frame):
+        _fail("The requested frame is missing")
+
+    result = Dataset()
+    if shared is not None:
+        for elem in shared[0]:
+            result.add(copy.deepcopy(elem))
+    for elem in per_frame[index]:
+        # Dataset assignment replaces by tag while retaining the position of
+        # a shared macro that it overrides.  This is also the natural DICOM
+        # meaning of a per-frame macro replacing a shared macro.
+        result.add(copy.deepcopy(elem))
+    return result
+
+
+def frame_attributes(ds: Dataset, index: int) -> Dataset:
+    """Return a copy of the functional group macros applying to one frame.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    ds : pydicom.dataset.Dataset
+        An enhanced multi-frame instance.
+    index : int
+        The zero-based frame index.
+    """
+    info = _validate(ds)
+    if not isinstance(index, Integral) or isinstance(index, bool):
+        _fail("The frame index is invalid")
+    return _frame_attributes_from_validated(info, int(index))
+
+
+def varying_attributes(ds: Dataset) -> set[BaseTag]:
+    """Return functional group macro tags whose effective value varies."""
+    info = _validate(ds)
+    if info.frame_count == 1:
+        return set()
+
+    frames = [
+        _frame_attributes_from_validated(info, index)
+        for index in range(info.frame_count)
+    ]
+    tags: list[BaseTag] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        for tag in frame.keys():
+            if tag not in tags:
+                tags.append(tag)
+
+    varying: set[BaseTag] = set()
+    for tag in tags:
+        first = frames[0]._dict.get(tag, _MISSING)
+        if any(
+            (value is _MISSING)
+            or (first is _MISSING)
+            or not _same_element(first, value)
+            for frame in frames[1:]
+            for value in [frame._dict.get(tag, _MISSING)]
+        ):
+            varying.add(tag)
+    return varying
+
+
+def _normalise_indices(indices: Iterable[int], frame_count: int) -> list[int]:
+    if isinstance(indices, (str, bytes)):
+        _fail("The frame selection is invalid")
+    try:
+        selected = list(indices)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The frame selection is invalid") from exc
+    if not selected:
+        _fail("The frame selection is empty")
+
+    result: list[int] = []
+    for value in selected:
+        if not isinstance(value, Integral) or isinstance(value, bool):
+            _fail("The frame selection contains an invalid index")
+        index = int(value)
+        if index < 0 or index >= frame_count:
+            _fail("The frame selection contains a missing frame")
+        if index in result:
+            _fail("The frame selection contains a repeated frame")
+        result.append(index)
+    return result
+
+
+def _sequence_key_list(keys: Iterable[Any]) -> list[BaseTag]:
+    if isinstance(keys, (str, BaseTag, int)):
+        raw_keys = [keys]
+    elif isinstance(keys, tuple) and len(keys) == 2 and all(
+        isinstance(value, int) for value in keys
+    ):
+        raw_keys = [keys]
+    else:
+        try:
+            raw_keys = list(keys)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("The keys are invalid") from exc
+    if not raw_keys:
+        _fail("At least one key is required")
+
+    result: list[BaseTag] = []
+    for key in raw_keys:
+        try:
+            if isinstance(key, str) and tag_for_keyword(key) is None:
+                # Tag() also accepts the conventional hexadecimal tag string,
+                # which is useful for private or not-yet-dictionary elements.
+                tag = Tag(key)
+            else:
+                tag = Tag(key)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("Each key must be an attribute name or tag") from exc
+        result.append(tag)
+    return result
+
+
+def _key_value(attributes: Dataset, tag: BaseTag) -> Any:
+    elem = attributes._dict.get(tag)
+    if elem is None or elem.is_empty:
+        return _MISSING
+    return elem.value
+
+
+def _sort_value(value: Any) -> Any:
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, Sequence)):
+        return tuple(_sort_value(item) for item in value)
+    if isinstance(value, Dataset):
+        return value
+    return value
+
+
+def _selected_frames(
+    info: _Validated, indices: Iterable[int]
+) -> list[_Selected]:
+    return [
+        _Selected(info, index, _frame_attributes_from_validated(info, index))
+        for index in indices
+    ]
+
+
+def _normalise_in_stack_positions(frames: list[_Selected]) -> None:
+    stacks: list[tuple[Any, list[_Selected]]] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        content_elem = frame.attributes._dict.get(_FRAME_CONTENT)
+        if content_elem is None:
+            continue
+        content_items = content_elem.value
+        if not isinstance(content_items, Sequence):
+            continue
+        position_items = [
+            item
+            for item in content_items
+            if isinstance(item, Dataset) and _IN_STACK_POSITION in item
+        ]
+        if not position_items:
+            continue
+        stack_value = _MISSING
+        if _STACK_ID in position_items[0]:
+            stack_value = position_items[0][_STACK_ID].value
+        for existing_value, members in stacks:
+            if _same_value(existing_value, stack_value):
+                members.append(frame)
+                break
+        else:
+            stacks.append((stack_value, [frame]))
+
+    for _, members in stacks:
+        for position, frame in enumerate(members, start=1):
+            content_elem = frame.attributes._dict.get(_FRAME_CONTENT)
+            if content_elem is None or not isinstance(content_elem.value, Sequence):
+                continue
+            for item in content_elem.value:
+                if isinstance(item, Dataset) and _IN_STACK_POSITION in item:
+                    item[_IN_STACK_POSITION].value = position
+
+
+def _dimension_values(frame: _Selected) -> tuple[Dataset, DataElement] | None:
+    content_elem = frame.attributes._dict.get(_FRAME_CONTENT)
+    if content_elem is None or not isinstance(content_elem.value, Sequence):
+        return None
+    for item in content_elem.value:
+        if not isinstance(item, Dataset):
+            continue
+        values = item._dict.get(_DIMENSION_VALUES)
+        if values is not None and not values.is_empty:
+            return item, values
+    return None
+
+
+def _normalise_dimensions(result: Dataset, frames: list[_Selected]) -> None:
+    value_frames: list[tuple[_Selected, Dataset, DataElement, list[Any]]] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        values = _dimension_values(frame)
+        if values is not None:
+            item, elem = values
+            value_frames.append((frame, item, elem, _parse_int_list(elem.value)))
+
+    if not value_frames:
+        dimension_elem = _get_element(result, _DIMENSION_INDEX)
+        if dimension_elem is not None and dimension_elem.is_empty:
+            del result[_DIMENSION_INDEX]
+        return
+
+    max_dimensions = max(len(values) for _, _, _, values in value_frames)
+    drop: set[int] = set()
+    for dimension in range(max_dimensions):
+        reached = [
+            values[dimension]
+            for _, _, _, values in value_frames
+            if len(values) > dimension
+        ]
+        if len(reached) == len(value_frames) and reached and all(
+            _same_value(reached[0], value) for value in reached[1:]
+        ):
+            drop.add(dimension)
+
+    kept = [dimension for dimension in range(max_dimensions) if dimension not in drop]
+    remapped: dict[int, list[Any]] = {dimension: [] for dimension in kept}
+    for _, _, _, values in value_frames:
+        for dimension in kept:
+            if dimension >= len(values):
+                continue
+            value = values[dimension]
+            if not any(_same_value(value, existing) for existing in remapped[dimension]):
+                remapped[dimension].append(value)
+
+    for _, item, elem, values in value_frames:
+        new_values: list[int] = []
+        for dimension in kept:
+            if dimension >= len(values):
+                continue
+            value = values[dimension]
+            number = next(
+                index
+                for index, existing in enumerate(remapped[dimension], start=1)
+                if _same_value(existing, value)
+            )
+            new_values.append(number)
+        if new_values:
+            elem.value = new_values
+        else:
+            del item[_DIMENSION_VALUES]
+
+    dimension_elem = _get_element(result, _DIMENSION_INDEX)
+    if dimension_elem is not None:
+        if dimension_elem.VR != "SQ" or not isinstance(dimension_elem.value, Sequence):
+            _fail("The Dimension Index Sequence is malformed")
+        dimension_items = list(dimension_elem.value)
+        kept_descriptions = [
+            item for index, item in enumerate(dimension_items) if index not in drop
+        ]
+        if kept_descriptions:
+            dimension_elem.value = Sequence(kept_descriptions)
+        else:
+            del result[_DIMENSION_INDEX]
+
+
+def _write_functional_groups(result: Dataset, frames: list[_Selected]) -> None:
+    tags: list[BaseTag] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        for tag in frame.attributes.keys():
+            if tag not in tags:
+                tags.append(tag)
+
+    shared = Dataset()
+    per_frame: list[Dataset] = [Dataset() for _ in frames]
+    for tag in tags:
+        values = [frame.attributes._dict.get(tag) for frame in frames]
+        first = values[0]
+        common = first is not None and all(
+            value is not None and _same_element(first, value) for value in values[1:]
+        )
+        if common:
+            shared.add(copy.deepcopy(first))
+        else:
+            for item, value in zip(per_frame, values):
+                if value is not None:
+                    item.add(copy.deepcopy(value))
+
+    result[_SHARED_FG] = DataElement(_SHARED_FG, "SQ", Sequence([shared]))
+    result[_PER_FRAME_FG] = DataElement(_PER_FRAME_FG, "SQ", Sequence(per_frame))
+
+
+def _write_pixel_data(
+    result: Dataset, selected: list[_Selected], first: _Validated
+) -> None:
+    frames = [frame.source.frames[frame.index] for frame in selected]
+    if first.encapsulated:
+        data = encapsulate(frames)
+    elif first.bit_frames:
+        bits = b"".join(frames)
+        packed = bytearray((len(bits) + 7) // 8)
+        for index, value in enumerate(bits):
+            if value:
+                packed[index // 8] |= 1 << (index % 8)
+        if len(packed) % 2:
+            packed.append(0)
+        data = bytes(packed)
+    else:
+        data = b"".join(frames)
+        if len(data) % 2:
+            data += b"\x00"
+
+    for tag in _PIXEL_TAGS:
+        if tag in result._dict and tag != first.pixel_tag:
+            del result[tag]
+    result[first.pixel_tag] = DataElement(
+        first.pixel_tag,
+        first.pixel_vr,
+        data,
+        is_undefined_length=first.encapsulated,
+    )
+    for tag in (_EXTENDED_OFFSET, _EXTENDED_LENGTHS):
+        if tag in result._dict:
+            del result[tag]
+
+
+def _write_source_images(
+    result: Dataset,
+    selected: list[_Selected],
+    sources: list[_Validated],
+) -> None:
+    sequence = Sequence()
+    for source_index, source in enumerate(sources):
+        frame_numbers = [
+            frame.index + 1
+            for frame in selected
+            if frame.source is source
+        ]
+        item = Dataset()
+        item.ReferencedSOPClassUID = copy.deepcopy(source.sop_class)
+        item.ReferencedSOPInstanceUID = copy.deepcopy(source.sop_instance)
+        item.ReferencedFrameNumber = frame_numbers
+        sequence.append(item)
+    result[_SOURCE_IMAGE] = DataElement(_SOURCE_IMAGE, "SQ", sequence)
+
+
+def _derive(sources: list[_Validated], selection: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> Dataset:
+    if not sources or not selection:
+        _fail("No frames were selected")
+
+    selected = [
+        _Selected(
+            sources[source_index],
+            frame_index,
+            _frame_attributes_from_validated(sources[source_index], frame_index),
+        )
+        for source_index, frame_index in selection
+    ]
+    result = copy.deepcopy(sources[0].dataset)
+    first = sources[0]
+
+    _normalise_in_stack_positions(selected)
+    _normalise_dimensions(result, selected)
+    _write_functional_groups(result, selected)
+    _write_pixel_data(result, selected, first)
+
+    result.NumberOfFrames = len(selected)
+    new_instance = generate_uid()
+    result.SOPInstanceUID = new_instance
+    result.ensure_file_meta()
+    result.file_meta.MediaStorageSOPClassUID = copy.deepcopy(result.SOPClassUID)
+    result.file_meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID = new_instance
+    _write_source_images(result, selected, sources)
+    return result
+
+
+def extract_frames(ds: Dataset, indices: Iterable[int]) -> Dataset:
+    """Return a derived instance containing the selected frames in order."""
+    info = _validate(ds)
+    selected = _normalise_indices(indices, info.frame_count)
+    return _derive([info], [(0, index) for index in selected])
+
+
+def _check_combinable(sources: list[_Validated]) -> None:
+    if not sources:

class PrivateBlock:
    """Helper class for a private block in the :class:`Dataset`.

    See the DICOM Standard, Part 5,
    :dcm:`Section 7.8.1<part05/sect_7.8.html#sect_7.8.1>` - Private Data
    Element Tags

    Attributes
    ----------
    group : int
        The private group where the private block is located as a 32-bit
        :class:`int`.
    private_creator : str
        The private creator string related to the block.
    dataset : Dataset
        The parent dataset.
    block_start : int
        The start element of the private block as a 32-bit :class:`int`. Note
        that the 2 low order hex digits of the element are always 0.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, key: tuple[int, str], dataset: "Dataset", private_creator_element: int
    ) -> None:
        """Initializes an object corresponding to a private tag block.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key : tuple
            The private (tag group, creator) as ``(int, str)``. The group
            must be an odd number.
        dataset : Dataset
            The parent :class:`Dataset`.
        private_creator_element : int
            The element of the private creator tag as a 32-bit :class:`int`.
        """
        self.group = key[0]
        self.private_creator = key[1]
        self.dataset = dataset
        self.block_start = private_creator_element << 8

    def get_tag(self, element_offset: int) -> BaseTag:
        """Return the private tag ID for the given `element_offset`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag.

        Returns
        -------
            The tag ID defined by the private block location and the
            given element offset.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        """
        if element_offset > 0xFF:
            raise ValueError("Element offset must be less than 256")
        return Tag(self.group, self.block_start + element_offset)

    def __contains__(self, element_offset: int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the tag with given `element_offset` is in
        the parent :class:`Dataset`.
        """
        return self.get_tag(element_offset) in self.dataset

    def __getitem__(self, element_offset: int) -> DataElement:
        """Return the data element in the parent dataset for the given element
        offset.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag.

        Returns
        -------
            The data element of the tag in the parent dataset defined by the
            private block location and the given element offset.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        KeyError
            If no data element exists at that offset.
        """
        return self.dataset.__getitem__(self.get_tag(element_offset))

    def __delitem__(self, element_offset: int) -> None:
        """Delete the tag with the given `element_offset` from the dataset.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag
            to be deleted.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        KeyError
            If no data element exists at that offset.
        """
        del self.dataset[self.get_tag(element_offset)]

    def add_new(self, element_offset: int, VR: str, value: object) -> None:
        """Add a private element to the parent :class:`Dataset`.

        Adds the private tag with the given `VR` and `value` to the parent
        :class:`Dataset` at the tag ID defined by the private block and the
        given `element_offset`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag
            to be added.
        VR : str
            The 2 character DICOM value representation.
        value
            The value of the data element. See :meth:`Dataset.add_new()`
            for a description.
        """
        tag = self.get_tag(element_offset)
        self.dataset.add_new(tag, VR, value)
        self.dataset[tag].private_creator = self.private_creator


def _dict_equal(a: "Dataset", b: Any, exclude: list[str] | None = None) -> bool:
    """Common method for Dataset.__eq__ and FileDataset.__eq__

    Uses .keys() as needed because Dataset iter return items not keys
    `exclude` is used in FileDataset__eq__ ds.__dict__ compare, which
    would also compare the wrapped _dict member (entire dataset) again.
    """
    return (
        len(a) == len(b)
        and all(key in b for key in a.keys())
        and all(
            a[key] == b[key]
            for key in a.keys()
            if exclude is None or key not in exclude
        )
    )

class Dataset:  # noqa: PLW1641
    """A DICOM dataset as a mutable mapping of DICOM Data Elements.

    Examples
    --------
    Add an element to the :class:`Dataset` (for elements in the DICOM
    dictionary):

    >>> ds = Dataset()
    >>> ds.PatientName = "CITIZEN^Joan"
    >>> ds.add_new(0x00100020, 'LO', '12345')
    >>> ds[0x0010, 0x0030] = DataElement(0x00100030, 'DA', '20010101')

    Add a sequence element to the :class:`Dataset`

    >>> ds.BeamSequence = [Dataset(), Dataset(), Dataset()]
    >>> ds.BeamSequence[0].Manufacturer = "Linac, co."
    >>> ds.BeamSequence[1].Manufacturer = "Linac and Sons, co."
    >>> ds.BeamSequence[2].Manufacturer = "Linac and Daughters, co."

    Add private elements to the :class:`Dataset`

    >>> block = ds.private_block(0x0041, 'My Creator', create=True)
    >>> block.add_new(0x01, 'LO', '12345')

    Updating and retrieving element values:

    >>> ds.PatientName = "CITIZEN^Joan"
    >>> ds.PatientName
    'CITIZEN^Joan'
    >>> ds.PatientName = "CITIZEN^John"
    >>> ds.PatientName
    'CITIZEN^John'

    Retrieving an element's value from a Sequence:

    >>> ds.BeamSequence[0].Manufacturer
    'Linac, co.'
    >>> ds.BeamSequence[1].Manufacturer
    'Linac and Sons, co.'

    Accessing the :class:`~pydicom.dataelem.DataElement` items:

    >>> elem = ds['PatientName']
    >>> elem
    (0010,0010) Patient's Name                      PN: 'CITIZEN^John'
    >>> elem = ds[0x00100010]
    >>> elem
    (0010,0010) Patient's Name                      PN: 'CITIZEN^John'
    >>> elem = ds.data_element('PatientName')
    >>> elem
    (0010,0010) Patient's Name                      PN: 'CITIZEN^John'

    Accessing a private :class:`~pydicom.dataelem.DataElement`
    item:

    >>> block = ds.private_block(0x0041, 'My Creator')
    >>> elem = block[0x01]
    >>> elem
    (0041,1001) Private tag data                    LO: '12345'
    >>> elem.value
    '12345'

    Alternatively:

    >>> ds.get_private_item(0x0041, 0x01, 'My Creator').value
    '12345'

    Deleting an element from the :class:`Dataset`

    >>> del ds.PatientID
    >>> del ds.BeamSequence[1].Manufacturer
    >>> del ds.BeamSequence[2]

    Deleting a private element from the :class:`Dataset`

    >>> block = ds.private_block(0x0041, 'My Creator')
    >>> if 0x01 in block:
    ...     del block[0x01]

    Determining if an element is present in the :class:`Dataset`

    >>> 'PatientName' in ds
    True
    >>> 'PatientID' in ds
    False
    >>> (0x0010, 0x0030) in ds
    True
    >>> 'Manufacturer' in ds.BeamSequence[0]
    True

    Iterating through the top level of a :class:`Dataset` only (excluding
    Sequences):

    >>> for elem in ds:
    ...    print(elem)
    (0010,0010) Patient's Name                      PN: 'CITIZEN^John'

    Iterating through the entire :class:`Dataset` (including Sequences):

    >>> for elem in ds.iterall():
    ...     print(elem)
    (0010,0010) Patient's Name                      PN: 'CITIZEN^John'

    Recursively iterate through a :class:`Dataset` (including Sequences):

    >>> def recurse(ds):
    ...     for elem in ds:
    ...         if elem.VR == 'SQ':
    ...             [recurse(item) for item in elem.value]
    ...         else:
    ...             # Do something useful with each DataElement

    >>> ds = Dataset()
    >>> ds.PatientName = "Some^Name"
    >>> jsonmodel = ds.to_json()

# Functions for parsing encapsulated data
def parse_basic_offsets(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> list[int]:
    """Return the encapsulated pixel data's basic offset table frame offsets.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the
        beginning of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then after reading it will be
        positioned at the start of the item tag of the first fragment after the
        Basic Offset Table.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    list[int]
        A list of the offset positions to the first item tag of each frame, as
        measured from the end of the basic offset table.

    References
    ----------
    :dcm:`DICOM Standard, Part 5, Annex A.4<part05/sect_A.4.html#table_A.4-1>`
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
    if group << 16 | elem != 0xFFFEE000:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Found unexpected tag {Tag(group, elem)} instead of (FFFE,E000) "
            "when parsing the Basic Offset Table item"
        )

    length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", buffer.read(4))[0]
    if length % 4:
        raise ValueError(
            "The length of the Basic Offset Table item is not a multiple of 4"
        )

    if length == 0:
        return []

    return list(unpack(f"{endianness}{length // 4}L", buffer.read(length)))


def parse_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> tuple[int, list[int]]:
    """Return the number of fragments and their positions in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, such as after the end of the Basic
        Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or an
        object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the latter
        then the offset will be reset to the starting position afterwards.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, list[int]]
        The number of fragments and the absolute offset position of the first
        byte of the item tag for each fragment in `buffer`.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    start_offset = buffer.tell()

    nr_fragments = 0
    fragment_offsets = []
    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )
            nr_fragments += 1
            fragment_offsets.append(buffer.tell() - 8)
            buffer.seek(length, 1)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )

    buffer.seek(start_offset, 0)

    return nr_fragments, fragment_offsets


def generate_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> Iterator[bytes]:
    """Yield frame fragments from the encapsulated pixel data in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, usually this will be after the end
        of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or
        an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the
        latter than the final offset position depends on how many fragments have
        been yielded.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    ------
    bytes
        A pixel data fragment.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )

            yield buffer.read(length)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )


def generate_fragmented_frames(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer,
    *,
    number_of_frames: int | None = None,
    extended_offsets: tuple[list[int], list[int]] | tuple[bytes, bytes] | None = None,
    endianness: str = "<",
) -> Iterator[tuple[bytes, ...]]:
    """Yield fragmented pixel data frames from `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    .. note::

        When the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset Table
        isn't supplied then more fragmented frames may be yielded than given
        by `number_of_frames` provided there are sufficient excess fragments
        available.

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the first
        byte of the basic offset table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then the final position depends on
        how many fragmented frames have been yielded.
    number_of_frames : int, optional
        Required when the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset Table
        has not been supplied. This should be the value of (0028,0008) *Number of
        Frames* or the expected number of frames in the encapsulated data.
    extended_offsets : tuple[list[int], list[int]] or tuple[bytes, bytes], optional
        The (offsets, lengths) of the Extended Offset Table as taken from
        (7FE0,0001) *Extended Offset Table* and (7FE0,0002) *Extended Offset
        Table Lengths* as either the raw encoded values or a list of their
        decoded equivalents.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    -------
    tuple[bytes, ...]
        An encapsulated pixel data frame, with the contents of the tuple the
        frame's fragmented encoded data.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    basic_offsets = parse_basic_offsets(buffer, endianness=endianness)
    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table

    # Prefer the extended offset table (if available)
    if extended_offsets:
        # PS3.3, C.7.6.3.1.8
        # Byte offsets to the first byte of the item tag of the first fragment
        #   of every frame, as measured from the first byte of the item tag
        #   following the Basic Offset Table, which *should* be empty
        # Only 1 fragment per frame is allowed (Table C.7-11a)
        if isinstance(extended_offsets[0], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[0]) // 8
            offsets = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[0]))
        else:
            offsets = extended_offsets[0]

        if isinstance(extended_offsets[1], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[1]) // 8
            lengths = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[1]))
        else:
            lengths = extended_offsets[1]

        fragments_start = buffer.tell()
        for offset, length in zip(offsets, lengths):
            # 8 for the item tag and item length, which we don't need
            buffer.seek(fragments_start + offset + 8, 0)
            yield (buffer.read(length),)

        return

    # Fall back to the basic offset table (if available)
    if basic_offsets:
        frame = []
        current_index = 0

def _array_common(
    f: BinaryIO, specific_tags: list[BaseTag | int], **kwargs: Any
) -> tuple["Dataset", dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return a dataset from `f` and a corresponding decoding options dict.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : BinaryIO
        The opened file-like containing the DICOM dataset, positioned at the
        start of the file.
    specific_tags : list[BaseTag | int]
        A list of additional tags to be read from the dataset and possibly
        returned via the `ds_out` dataset.
    kwargs : dict[str, Any]
        Required and optional arguments for the pixel data decoding functions.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[Dataset, dict[str, Any]]

        * A dataset containing the group 0x0028 elements, the extended offset
          elements (if any) and elements from `specific_tags`.
        * The required and optional arguments for the pixel data decoding
          functions.
    """
    from pydicom.filereader import (
        read_preamble,
        _read_file_meta_info,
        read_dataset,
        _at_pixel_data,
    )

    # Read preamble (if present)
    read_preamble(f, force=True)

    # Read the File Meta (if present)
    file_meta = _read_file_meta_info(f)
    tsyntax = kwargs.setdefault(
        "transfer_syntax_uid",
        file_meta.get("TransferSyntaxUID", None),
    )
    if not tsyntax:
        raise AttributeError(
            "'transfer_syntax_uid' is required if the dataset in 'src' is not "
            "in the DICOM File Format"
        )

    tsyntax = UID(tsyntax)

    # Get the *Image Pixel* module 0028 elements, any extended offsets and
    #   any other tags wanted by the user
    ds = read_dataset(
        f,
        is_implicit_VR=tsyntax.is_implicit_VR,
        is_little_endian=tsyntax.is_little_endian,
        stop_when=_at_pixel_data,
        specific_tags=specific_tags,
    )
    ds.file_meta = file_meta

    opts = as_pixel_options(ds, **kwargs)
    opts["transfer_syntax_uid"] = tsyntax

    # We are either at the start of the element tag for a pixel data
    #   element or at EOF because there were none
    try:
        data = f.read(8)
        assert len(data) == 8
    except Exception:
        raise AttributeError(
            "The dataset in 'src' has no 'Pixel Data', 'Float Pixel Data' or "
            "'Double Float Pixel Data' element, no pixel data to decode"
        )

    endianness = "><"[tsyntax.is_little_endian]
    if tsyntax.is_implicit_VR:
        vr = None
        group, elem, length = unpack(f"{endianness}HHL", data)
    else:
        # Is always 32-bit extended length for pixel data VRs
        group, elem, vr, length = unpack(f"{endianness}HH2sH", data)
        opts["pixel_vr"] = vr.decode(default_encoding)
        unpack(f"{endianness}L", f.read(4))

    # We should now be positioned at the start of the pixel data value
    opts["pixel_keyword"] = _PIXEL_KEYWORDS[(group, elem)]

    return ds, opts


def as_pixel_options(ds: "Dataset", **kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a dict containing the image pixel element values from `ds`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds : pydicom.dataset.Dataset
        A dataset containing Image Pixel module elements.
    **kwargs
        A :class:`dict` containing (key, value) pairs to be used to override the
        values taken from `ds`. For example, if ``kwargs = {'rows': 64}`` then
        the returned :class:`dict` will have a 'rows' value of 64 rather than
        whatever ``ds.Rows`` may be.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, Any]
        A dictionary which may contain the following keys, depending on which
        elements are present in `ds` and the contents of `kwargs`:

        * `samples_per_pixel`
        * `photometric_interpretation`
        * `planar_configuration`
        * `number_of_frames` (always present)
        * `rows`
        * `columns`
        * `bits_allocated`
        * `bits_stored`
        * `pixel_representation`
    """
    opts = {
        attr: ds[tag].value for tag, attr in _IMAGE_PIXEL.items() if tag in ds._dict
    }

    # Ensure we have a valid 'number_of_frames'
    if 0x00280008 not in ds._dict:
        opts["number_of_frames"] = 1

    nr_frames = opts["number_of_frames"]
    nr_frames = int(nr_frames) if isinstance(nr_frames, str) else nr_frames
    if nr_frames in (None, 0):
        warn_and_log(
            f"A value of '{nr_frames}' for (0028,0008) 'Number of Frames' is invalid, "
            "assuming 1 frame"
        )
        nr_frames = 1

    opts["number_of_frames"] = nr_frames

    # Extended Offset Table
    if 0x7FE00001 in ds._dict and 0x7FE00001 in ds._dict:
        opts["extended_offsets"] = (
            ds.ExtendedOffsetTable,
            ds.ExtendedOffsetTableLengths,
        )

    opts.update(kwargs)

    return opts

    private_creator: str, new_entries_dict: dict[int, tuple[str, str, str, str]]

    """Update pydicom's private DICOM tag dictionary with new entries.

    Parameters
    ----------
    private_creator: str

    new_entries_dict : dict
        :class:`dict` of form ``{tag: (VR, VM, description, is_retired), ...}``
        where parameters are as described in :func:`add_private_dict_entry`.

    Raises
    ------

        If one of the entries is a non-private tag.

    --------

        Function to add a single entry to the private tag dictionary.

    Examples
    --------

    ...        0x00410001: ('UL', '1', "Test One"),
    ...        0x00410002: ('DS', '3', "Test Two", '3'),
    ... }
    >>> add_private_dict_entries("ACME LTD 1.2", new_dict_items)
    >>> add_private_dict_entry("ACME LTD 1.3", 0x00410001, "US", "Test Three")

    if not all([BaseTag(tag).is_private for tag in new_entries_dict]):
        raise ValueError(
            "Non-private tags cannot be added using "
            "'add_private_dict_entries()' - use 'add_dict_entries()' instead"
        )

    new_entries = {

The 4 bytes of the DICOM tag are stored as an 'int'. Tags are

from contextlib import contextmanager
import traceback
from typing import Any, TypeAlias
from collections.abc import Iterator


@contextmanager
def tag_in_exception(tag: "BaseTag") -> Iterator[None]:
    """Use `tag` within a context.

    Used to include the tag details in the traceback message when an exception
    is raised within the context.

    Note: It is preferable to use the `with dataset` context manager
    which provides the full path to the data element.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tag : BaseTag
        The tag to use in the context.
    """
    try:
        yield
    except Exception as exc:
        stack_trace = traceback.format_exc()
        msg = f"With tag {tag} got exception: {exc}\n{stack_trace}"
        raise type(exc)(msg) from exc


# Type that can be used where a parameter is a tag or keyword
TagType: TypeAlias = "int | str | tuple[int, int] | BaseTag"
TagListType = list[int] | list[str] | list[tuple[int, int]] | list["BaseTag"]


def Tag(arg: TagType, arg2: int | None = None) -> "BaseTag":
    """Create a :class:`BaseTag`.

    General function for creating a :class:`BaseTag` from any of the standard
    forms:

    * ``Tag(0x00100015)``
    * ``Tag((0x10, 0x50))``
    * ``Tag(0x0010, 0x0015)``
    * ``Tag("PatientName")``

    Parameters
    ----------
    arg : int | str | tuple[int, int]

        * If :class:`int` then either the group number or the combined
          group and element numbers of the tag
        * If :class:`str` then the corresponding element's keyword
        * If :class:`tuple` then the (group, element) numbers as
          (:class:`int`, :class:`int`).
    arg2 : int, optional
        The element number of the DICOM tag, required when `arg` only contains
        the group number of the tag.

    Returns
    -------
    BaseTag
    """
    if isinstance(arg, BaseTag):
        return arg

    if arg2 is not None:
        # act as if was passed a single tuple
        arg = (arg, arg2)  # type: ignore[assignment]

    long_value: int | None
    if isinstance(arg, tuple | list):
        if len(arg) != 2:
            raise ValueError("Tag must be an int or a 2-tuple")

        valid = False
        if isinstance(arg[0], str):
            valid = isinstance(arg[1], str)
            if valid:
                arg = (int(arg[0], 16), int(arg[1], 16))
        elif isinstance(arg[0], int):
            valid = isinstance(arg[1], int)
        if not valid:
            raise TypeError(
                f"Unable to create an element tag from '{arg}': both "
                "arguments must be the same type and str or int"
            )

        if arg[0] > 0xFFFF or arg[1] > 0xFFFF:
            raise OverflowError(
                f"Unable to create an element tag from '{arg}': the group "
                "and element values are limited to a maximum of 2-bytes each"
            )

        long_value = (arg[0] << 16) | arg[1]

    # Single str parameter
    elif isinstance(arg, str):
        try:
            long_value = int(arg, 16)
            if long_value > 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise OverflowError(
                    f"Unable to create an element tag from '{long_value}': "
                    "the combined group and element values  are limited to a "
                    "maximum of 4-bytes"
                )
        except ValueError:
            # Try a DICOM keyword
            from pydicom.datadict import tag_for_keyword

            long_value = tag_for_keyword(arg)
            if long_value is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Unable to create an element tag from '{arg}': "
                    "unknown DICOM element keyword or an invalid int"
                )
    # Single int parameter
    else:
        long_value = arg
        if long_value > 0xFFFFFFFF:
            raise OverflowError(
                f"Unable to create an element tag from '{long_value}': the "
                "combined group and element values are limited to a maximum "
                "of 4-bytes"
            )

    if long_value < 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unable to create an element tag from '{long_value}': tags must "
            "be positive"
        )

    return BaseTag(long_value)


class BaseTag(int):
    """Represents a DICOM element (group, element) tag.

    Tags are represented as an :class:`int`.
    """

    # Override comparisons so can convert "other" to Tag as necessary
    #   See Ordering Comparisons at:
    #   https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.0.html#ordering-comparisons
    def __le__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self`  is less than or equal to `other`."""
        return self == other or self < other

    def __lt__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` is less than `other`."""
        # Check if comparing with another Tag object; if not, create a temp one
        if not isinstance(other, int):
            try:
                other = Tag(other)
            except Exception:
                raise TypeError("Cannot compare Tag with non-Tag item")

        return int(self) < int(other)

    def __ge__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` is greater than or equal to `other`."""
        return self == other or self > other

    def __gt__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` is greater than `other`."""
        return not (self == other or self < other)

    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` equals `other`."""
        # Check if comparing with another Tag object; if not, create a temp one
        if not isinstance(other, int):
            try:
                other = Tag(other)
            except Exception:
                return False

        return int(self) == int(other)

    def __ne__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` does not equal `other`."""
        return not self == other

    # For python 3, any override of __cmp__ or __eq__
    # immutable requires explicit redirect of hash function
    # to the parent class
    #   See https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__hash__
    __hash__ = int.__hash__

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """Return the tag value as a hex string '(gggg,eeee)'."""
        return f"({self.group:04X},{self.element:04X})"

        # Only 1 fragment per frame is allowed (Table C.7-11a)

            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[1]) // 8

        "Unable to generate frames from the encapsulated pixel data as there "
        "are fewer fragments than frames; the dataset may be corrupt or the "
        "number of frames may be incorrect"

        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the first

        starting position if the frame was
        returned successfully.
    index : int
        The index of the frame to be returned, starting at ``0`` for the first
        frame.
    number_of_frames : int, optional

        the Extended Offset Table has not been supplied and there are
        multiple frames. This should be the value of (0028,0008) *Number of
        Frames* or the expected number of frames in the encapsulated data.
    extended_offsets : tuple[list[int], list[int]] or tuple[bytes, bytes], optional
        The (offsets, lengths) of the Extended Offset Table as taken from
        (7FE0,0001) *Extended Offset Table* and (7FE0,0002) *Extended Offset
        Table Lengths* as either the raw encoded values or a list of their
        decoded equivalents.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    bytes
        A single frame of encoded pixel data.


    References
    ----------
    DICOM Standard Part 5, :dcm:`Annex A <part05/chapter_A.html>`
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    # `buffer` is positioned at the start of the basic offsets table
    starting_position = buffer.tell()

    basic_offsets = parse_basic_offsets(buffer, endianness=endianness)
    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table

    # Prefer the extended offset table (if available)
    if extended_offsets:
        if isinstance(extended_offsets[0], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[0]) // 8
            offsets = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[0]))
        else:
            offsets = extended_offsets[0]

        if isinstance(extended_offsets[1], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[1]) // 8
            lengths = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[1]))
        else:
            lengths = extended_offsets[1]

        if index >= len(offsets):
            raise ValueError(
                "There aren't enough offsets in the Extended Offset Table for "
                f"{index + 1} frames"
            )

        # We have the length so skip past the item tag and item length
        buffer.seek(offsets[index] + 8, 1)
        frame = buffer.read(lengths[index])
        buffer.seek(starting_position)
        return frame

    # Fall back to the basic offset table (if available)
    if basic_offsets:
        if index >= len(basic_offsets):
            raise ValueError(
                "There aren't enough offsets in the Basic Offset Table for "
                f"{index + 1} frames"
            )

        # There may be multiple fragments per frame
        if index < len(basic_offsets) - 1:
            # N - 1th frames
            length = basic_offsets[index + 1] - basic_offsets[index]
            buffer.seek(basic_offsets[index], 1)
            fragments = generate_fragments(buffer.read(length), endianness=endianness)
        else:
            # Final frame
            buffer.seek(basic_offsets[-1], 1)
            fragments = generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)

        frame = b"".join(fragment for fragment in fragments)
        buffer.seek(starting_position)
        return frame

    # No basic or extended offset table
    # Determine the number of fragments in `buffer` an their offsets
    nr_fragments, fragment_offsets = parse_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)
    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table

    # Single fragment must be 1 frame
    if nr_fragments == 1:
        if index == 0:
            frame = next(generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness))
            buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
            return frame

        raise ValueError(
            "Found 1 frame fragment in the encapsulated pixel data, 'index' must be 0"
        )

    # From this point on we require the number of frames as there are
    #   multiple fragments and may be one or more frames
    if not number_of_frames:
        raise ValueError(
            "Unable to determine the frame boundaries for the encapsulated "
            "pixel data as there is no basic or extended offset table data and "
            "the number of frames has not been supplied"
        )

    # 1 fragment per frame, for N frames
    if nr_fragments == number_of_frames:
        if index > nr_fragments - 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Found {nr_fragments} frame fragments in the encapsulated "
                f"pixel data, an 'index' of {index} is invalid"
            )

        # Covers RLE and others if 1:1 ratio
        # `fragment_offsets` is the absolute positions of each item tag
        buffer.seek(fragment_offsets[index], 0)
        frame = next(generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness))
        buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
        return frame

    fragments = generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)

    # Multiple fragments for 1 frame
    if number_of_frames == 1:
        if index == 0:
            frame = b"".join(fragment for fragment in fragments)
            buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
            return frame

        raise ValueError("The 'index' must be 0 if the number of frames is 1")

    # Search for JPEG/JPEG-LS/JPEG2K EOI/EOC marker which should be the
    #   last two bytes of a frame
    eoi_marker = b"\xff\xd9"
    frame_fragments = []
    frame_nr = 0
    for fragment in fragments:
        frame_fragments.append(fragment)
        if eoi_marker in fragment[-10:]:
            if frame_nr == index:
                frame = b"".join(frame_fragments)
                buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
                return frame

            frame_nr += 1
            frame_fragments = []

    if frame_fragments and index == frame_nr:
        warn_and_log(
            "The end of the encapsulated pixel data has been reached but no "
            "JPEG EOI/EOC marker was found, the returned frame data may be "
            "invalid"
        )
        frame = b"".join(frame_fragments)
        buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
        return frame

    raise ValueError(f"There is insufficient pixel data to contain {index + 1} frames")
